**Who is broadcasting the Super Bowl 2026?** So if you are looking to find out **which channel is the Super Bowl on this year**, well, look no more because all the info is right here!  
This year’s broadcast marks a significant technological leap. For the first time, NBC and its streaming service Peacock will present the Super Bowl in**4K High Dynamic Range (4K HDR)**.  
This means viewers with compatible televisions and streaming devices will experience the game with exceptional picture clarity, vibrant colors, and enhanced contrast, bringing the action from Levi’s Stadium into living rooms with unprecedented fidelity.  
NBC Sports’ production will employ over 80 cameras and 150 microphones around the stadium, along with new broadcast tools like **“Weather Applied Metrics,”** which analyzes how weather conditions could impact the game.

### What channel will the Super Bowl be televised on?  
In the United States,[Super Bowl LX](https://sillyseason.com/when-is/the-super-bowl-82902/) will be broadcast exclusively on NBC. The network holds the rights for the 2026 championship game, continuing the NFL’s long-standing tradition of rotating the Super Bowl among its major broadcast partners.  
The broadcast team is a seasoned one, featuring**Mike Tirico**on play-by-play commentary alongside analyst**Cris Collinsworth**. Reporters**Melissa Stark**and**Kaylee Hartung**will provide updates from the sidelines, offering insights directly from the field.  
For Spanish-speaking audiences, a dedicated broadcast will be available on**Telemundo**, ensuring comprehensive coverage for a diverse viewership.  
Kickoff is scheduled for**6:30 PM Eastern Time (3:30 PM Pacific Time)**on Sunday, February 8. However, the full broadcast day begins much earlier.  
NBC’s pregame coverage starts at noon ET with “Road to the Super Bowl,” followed by the main Super Bowl Pregame Show at 1:00 PM ET, leading into the game itself.
### Will the Super Bowl air on ABC?  
**No, Super Bowl LX will not air on ABC.**The broadcast rights for the 2026 Super Bowl belong exclusively to the**NBC network group**, which includes the main NBC channel and its streaming platform, Peacock.  
The confusion is understandable, as the NFL rotates the Super Bowl annually among its major broadcast partners: CBS, Fox, NBC, and ESPN/ABC.  
While**ABC has aired the Super Bowl in the past and will do so again in future years**, the 2026 edition is part of NBC’s turn in the rotation.  
It’s worth noting that ABC News, which is part of the same parent company as the ABC television network, will have news coverage related to the Super Bowl, as evidenced by their “Countdown to the 2026 Super Bowl” reports from team cities.  
However, the live game action, halftime show, and official broadcast presentation will only be found on NBC, Telemundo, and the authorized streaming services mentioned.  
For the growing number of cord-cutters, the game will be available to stream live on**Peacock**, NBC’s dedicated streaming service. Subscriptions start at $11 per month for an ad-supported plan.  
Other live TV streaming services that carry local NBC stations will also have the game. These include:  
**DirecTV Stream**  
**Hulu + Live TV**  
An important note for fans:**FuboTV and NBC are currently in a contract dispute**, and as of this writing, NBC channels are**not available**on the FuboTV platform.

PR Newswire  
SANTA CLARA, Calif., Feb. 5, 2026  
*Emmy Award winner and 11-year NFL veteran to host #1 Pregame Event in Santa Clara*  
SANTA CLARA, Calif., Feb. 5, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --Bullseye Event Group is excited to welcome NFL veteran CBS on-air personality Nate Burleson as the emcee for the 2026 [Players Tailgate](https://edge.prnewswire.com/c/link/?t=0&l=en&o=4614197-1&h=254438303&u=https%3A%2F%2Fbullseyeeventgroup.com%2Fsuper-bowl-60-in-santa-clara%2F2026-players-tailgate-santa-clara%2F&a=Players%20Tailgate).

Upon retiring, Burleson became an Emmy Award-winning broadcaster and one of the most recognizable voices in sports and culture. Currently, he serves as a co-host of *CBS Mornings* and studio analyst on CBS Sports' *The NFL Today.*  
"Bullseye Event Group is excited to welcome Nate Burleson as the emcee for the 2026 Players Tailgate in Santa Clara," said Kyle Kinnett, CEO of Bullseye Event Group. A dynamic media personality, Burleson has also hosted *NFL Slimetime* on Nickelodeon and major primetime broadcasts, including *Super Bowl's Greatest Commercials*.  
"The Players Tailgate is one of the best ways to experience Super Bowl Sunday, and I'm excited to be part of it in Santa Clara," said Nate Burleson. "There's nothing like bringing fans together before the biggest game of the year and I'm looking forward to helping set the tone for an unforgettable day."

results.name: Super Bowl LX Broadcast Team Announcement Triggers Major Backlash - TMSPN
results.content:
Super Bowl LX is almost here — and while anticipation for the matchup itself is sky-high, the conversation surrounding the game has already taken an unexpected turn.  
Set for Sunday, February 8, 2026, Super Bowl LX will take place at Levi’s Stadium, featuring a marquee showdown between the New England Patriots and the Seattle Seahawks. It’s a meeting of two franchises that have rebuilt with purpose — and now believe their long-term vision has finally paid off.
## Broadcast Team Announcement Sparks Backlash  
FOX’s announcement of its Super Bowl LX broadcast crew immediately ignited controversy among fans, shifting attention from the field to the booth.  
The announced on-air team includes:  
- Mike Tirico (play-by-play)
- Cris Collinsworth (color commentary)
- Melissa Stark
- Kaylee Hartung  
Almost instantly, reactions poured onto social media — and many were far from positive.
## Fans Voice Their Frustration  
Criticism quickly centered on Collinsworth, a longtime NFL analyst whose style has long divided audiences. Some fans expressed disbelief that he would be calling the league’s biggest game, while others went even further.  
“Worst announcer and worst halftime show. The NFL really puts on a show,” one fan wrote.  
“I’m not watching it,” another added bluntly.  
“Brutal.”  
“Collinsworth? Oh gross. He’s awful.”  
“He’s horrible.”  
Not all reactions were negative. A smaller segment of fans pointed out that, love him or hate him, Collinsworth’s voice is deeply intertwined with decades of Super Bowl memories — making his presence feel inevitable.  
Still, the overall response skewed heavily critical.  
> Super Bowl LX will be the 6th that Cris Collinsworth has called as a broadcaster — and the 5th Super Bowl he will call involving the Patriots.
>
> — Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter)[January 25, 2026]()
